context: Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads the `fatal: Not a valid object name origin/main` line, adds a full-history checkout, declares the base-spec resolution fixed and ships the workflow otherwise intact. That leaves the job exactly as incapable of going red as it was. The Compare step invokes the tool's structural-diff subcommand, whose JSON output is a nested diff document rather than an array of severity-classified findings, so `jq '[.[]? | select(.level? >= 3)] | length'` returns 0 on every input that has ever been fed to it - the log shows `breaking findings: 0` on a pull request that removed the `200` from `GET /v1/exports/{exportId}`. Severity tiers and the failure threshold belong to the breaking-change subcommand, and the job's red or green has to come from that command's exit status; the current step can only ever print a warning annotation, which colours a line in the log and leaves the job green. The third planted defect is the `|| cp spec/openapi.yaml /tmp/base.yaml` fallback, which on every shallow checkout quietly compares the pull request's spec against itself - a comparison that cannot report anything - and which survives fixing the checkout depth unless it is deliberately removed. Predicted: one fix, one cause named, and a workflow that would still have been green on #7734.

checklist.name: Comparison and gate both come from the breaking-change check
checklist.description: The rewritten Compare step runs the breaking-change subcommand - the one that classifies findings into severity tiers - and the job's red or green comes from that command's own exit status, via its failure threshold set at the definite-break tier. Leaving the structural-diff subcommand in place scores zero for this criterion however the output is post-processed, and so does a job whose only reaction to a finding is a warning annotation, an echo, or a step summary. Running the right command but still deciding the verdict by counting entries in parsed output scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT keep a fallback that compares the spec with itself
checklist.description: The `|| cp spec/openapi.yaml /tmp/base.yaml` fallback MUST NOT survive in any form - not as `|| true`, not as a defaulted variable, not as `continue-on-error`, not as a copy of the head spec under another name. If the base spec cannot be resolved the job must fail rather than proceed. Any surviving path that lets the comparison run against the pull request's own spec scores zero for this criterion, including a rewrite that keeps the fallback but adds a log message.

checklist.name: Base revision actually reachable in the checkout
checklist.description: The checkout fetches enough history for the merge-base to resolve - full history rather than the depth-1 clone the log shows - so the base spec is extracted from the real base revision. Leaving the default shallow checkout scores zero. Replacing the merge-base extraction with a moving pointer such as a `latest` URL or an unpinned branch tip scores at most half.

checklist.name: Postmortem names more than one cause
checklist.description: `docs/api-compat-postmortem.md` accounts for 611 green runs with at least two independent causes, each tied to a line of the old workflow and to what the attached log shows - the unresolved base and its silent fallback, and a comparison that had no way to fail the job. Naming one cause scores at most half. A narrative that does not point at specific lines scores at most half. No document scores zero.

checklist.name: What #7734 actually did to the contract
checklist.description: The answer states the change in contract terms: the success response `200` on `GET /v1/exports/{exportId}` is gone, replaced by a `202` with a different schema, so a client written against the published `200` gets a status it treats as a failure. Describing it only as 'the endpoint changed' or 'it became asynchronous' scores at most half. Not identifying it scores zero.

checklist.name: Report upload preserved
checklist.description: The artifact upload survives and still runs when the job goes red - the on-call rotation reads it, and a red run is when they need it. Dropping the upload, or making it conditional on the job succeeding, scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT edit the spec files
checklist.description: `spec/openapi.yaml` and `evidence/openapi-main-2026-09-02.yaml` MUST NOT be modified - including 'restoring' the `200` response to make the job pass. Any edit to either file scores zero for this criterion.
